source.title: Frequency Regularization: Unveiling the Spectral Inductive Bias of Deep Neural Networks

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper; no material cutoff or garbling is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares dropout with an unregularized baseline on CIFAR-10 and reports lower test accuracy with dropout, challenging V6 in this tested setting. Its spectral measurements do not measure the train–test gap.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test accuracy and spectral suppression for three regularization conditions. The spectral suppression results are not measurements of the train–test gap and do not establish that a property tracks that gap. The robustness results concern blur and Gaussian noise, which are out of distribution and excluded from the mapped versions.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares dropout with no dropout on held-out CIFAR-10 images using ResNet-18, a new setting for V6. Its single strong-dropout configuration identifies a scope condition rather than refuting the claim that suitably configured dropout helps in some regimes.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the reported accuracy and spectral comparisons, but incompletely summarizes the authors' conclusion. They argue that L2's low-frequency filtering explains improved generalization and produces a trade-off between better resolution-loss robustness and worse Gaussian-noise robustness. The reported comparisons do not establish that causal explanation.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10 with standard augmentation, SGD, 50 epochs, and dropout p = 0.5 after convolutional blocks. It does not establish that this matches the original dropout study's recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: Regularization condition changes the reported SSR and final test accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: First-layer SSR is −4.463 without regularization, −1.397 with L2, and −1.598 with dropout.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: L2 and dropout suppress first-layer high-frequency energy growth in this ResNet-18 training setup.

fits_no_version.finding: L2 reaches 94.46% clean test accuracy versus 92.03% for baseline; the text also reports better low-resolution robustness but faster degradation under Gaussian noise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: L2 improves clean accuracy and robustness to resolution loss in this setting while worsening robustness to Gaussian noise.

fits_no_version.finding: The synthetic MLP experiment reports frequency-dependent suppression with L2 and reduced low-frequency fitting under strong L2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: L2 strength changes frequency-component fitting in a synthetic regression task.

record.problems: Only ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10 is tested; the paper states that SSR analyzes only the first convolutional layer. No uncertainty estimates are reported. The study does not measure the train–test gap, and its claims about generalization benefit are not established by the reported test-accuracy comparison alone.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and matched natural-label versus random-label held-out performance.
Width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the role of local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and the effects of tuning or optimizer adaptations.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Suitably tuned dropout rates, dropout-induced underfitting, very small training sets, fully connected classifiers, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay with augmentation.
Magnitude-aware weight perturbations, training–test gaps, and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus removing equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for V6. Its spectral measurements do not test V7. No uncertainty estimates are reported, so the 0.38-point dropout accuracy decrease is descriptive. L2 accuracy, synthetic fitting, and corruption results fit no listed version and therefore do not require missing entries.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural labels.
Network-width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Large versus small batch comparisons and recipe adaptations.
Very small training sets; fully connected classifiers; joint removal of dropout and weight decay with data augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples and comparing with random-example removal.

rows.subject: Baseline (No Reg)
rows.operation_detail: Measured Spectral Suppression Ratio (SSR) after training without weight decay or dropout.
rows.note: SSR measures high-frequency energy growth relative to initialization, not the train–test gap.
rows.check: SSR measures first-layer high-frequency energy growth, not any claimed effect in V1–V8. The reported value is correct.

rows.subject: L2 (10−3 )
rows.operation_detail: Trained with weight decay = 1 × 10−3 and measured SSR.
rows.note: The paper reports this as a 3.2× reduction in high-frequency growth compared with baseline; it is not a train–test-gap measure.
rows.check: The value and baseline are correct, but spectral suppression cannot establish any version's effect; replace observed with cannot_determine.

rows.subject: Dropout (p = 0.5)
rows.operation_detail: Trained with dropout after convolutional blocks and measured SSR.
rows.note: The paper reports this as 2.8× suppression compared with baseline; it is not a train–test-gap measure.
rows.check: The value and baseline are correct. Dropout's spectral suppression does not measure its effect on held-out error; replace observed with cannot_determine.

rows.subject: Baseline (No Reg)
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated final test accuracy after training without weight decay or dropout.
rows.note: Reference condition for the dropout comparison.
rows.check: Correct reference accuracy, but the control alone cannot establish dropout's effect.

rows.subject: Dropout (p = 0.5)
rows.operation_detail: Added dropout after convolutional blocks and evaluated final test accuracy.
rows.note: Accuracy is lower than baseline; the authors describe dropout's accuracy as lower.
rows.check: Correct: dropout accuracy is 91.65% versus 92.03% without regularization, a decrease of 0.38 percentage points. No uncertainty or dropout-rate sweep is reported.

relationships.condition: ResNet-18 on augmented CIFAR-10, 50 epochs of momentum SGD, dropout p=0.5 after convolutional blocks.
relationships.reason: R4 and R5 show accuracy falling from 92.03% to 91.65% with strong dropout. This configuration provides no benefit; without tuning or training-error results, it does not establish failure of suitably configured dropout or demonstrate underfitting.
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy fell from 92.03% to 91.65%, without uncertainty estimates. Dropout was not tuned, and underfitting remained unclear because the study provided no supporting training-error evidence.
